title: Tooling: exact eligibility masks accelerate historical reclamation
body:
The historical joint-dual compiler repeatedly visits retired slots whose frames cannot serve the requested region. This opt-in, source-pinned adapter uses exact coordinate-membership masks to remove those visits while preserving the complete eligible order, clearing XORs, paid frames and serialized words.

**Tooling improvement; no new κ.** Compilation is **4.53–4.87× faster than Chafik Boukhalfa's archived PR175 bucket optimization**, and **12.50–14.28× faster than the base compiler**, on the two shipped axes. PR175 already solves repeated sorting; this contribution adds geometry filtering and compares against its exact source bytes.

Three cyclic-order rounds on CPython 3.14.6 / macOS arm64, sequential fresh processes:

| Axis | Base compilation | PR175 buckets | Coordinate masks |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| h=23 | 54.310 s | 19.668 s | 4.346 s |
| h=25 | 93.476 s | 31.894 s | 6.548 s |

The complete measured process, including source admission, serialization, independent dirty-basis replay and transition reconstruction, improves 3.02–3.30× relative to PR175. Raw wall/CPU samples, source and implementation hashes, preliminary probes, and the separate successful public reproduction are retained. These are local historical-verifier measurements.

Validation:

- All 18 primary and six public-reproduction timing processes reproduce both frozen words byte for byte after decompression, and match every compiler, independent replay and transition receipt field.
- Untimed sorted-set audits compare the entire eligible sequence at all **71,519 acquisition requests**, including candidates beyond the chosen one.
- **12 focused tests and 16 unchanged historical controls pass.** Controls cover stale frame updates/removals, incorrect geometry/rank masks, source drift, disabled assertions, unpaid scatter, missing XORs/transitions and understated width. A deliberately omitted update hook fails real compilation.
- The selected-record/source-inventory check, measured implementation hashes and staged whitespace check pass. Existing sources, manifests, certificates, default commands and `upstream/` are unchanged.

Reproduce with standard-library Python 3.11+, from a full checkout and using a fresh output directory:

```sh
python3 -B research/reclamation-priority-performance/verify.py --out /tmp/reclamation-review
```

Expected final marker: `PASS_RECLAMATION_PRIORITY`. [Review map, proof and evidence](https://github.com/PeterCarp320/integer-mult-bounds/blob/daa9b0e773b53f36d5b4c3f1c7524600e5714deb/research/reclamation-priority-performance/README.md).

Exact base: `66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60`. OS-random assignment seed: **85**, verification engineering. No sprint coordination issue exists; the claim and scope refinement are recorded locally. Final overlap checks cover 586 open PRs through #767 plus arrivals through #772. Recent tooling #736/#752/#756 addresses different workloads. PR175 at `f1081fabbfadaaaaf7292a40d428dbbb865ce920` is the credited, incorporated predecessor and comparator.

The full repository suite, selected cold supplier replay, C++ CRT profiles, assembly and Lean were not rerun for this isolated adapter. Remote CI is separate from local verification. Inherited all-size/compiler/physical/hosting/precision/tape/analytic obligations remain; this is not a formal multiplication theorem.

Prepared for **Peter Carpenter** with substantial **OpenAI Codex** assistance. Credit eumemic's compiler and PR154 bottleneck report, Chafik Boukhalfa's ranked reclamation and PR175, Rohan Gupta's PR55 producer, rfu08's PR64 regression work and the retained predecessor lineage. Apache-2.0; full attribution and AI disclosure are in `NOTICE.md`.
